title: Accelerate safe rollback & incremental CR resync for failed on-prem Helm upgrades
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: A Tier-1 customer running Redwood Private experienced repeated post-upgrade failures after a weekend operator/Helm rollout. Symptoms: tenants reporting inference pod flapping, operator stuck reconciling same CRs, and long KV cache schema mismatch errors. Root cause: partial Helm hooks execution + race between operator preflight validators and tenant manifest projection resulted in inconsistent CR state and orphaned KV entries. Impact: several dedicated tenants degraded for 30-90 minutes during peak traffic; multiple escalations to SE and SRE.
detailed_scope: This ticket implements a surgical hotfix (operator 2.7.4) that: 1) adds a 'rollback-accelerator' code path to detect partially-applied Helm releases via release-checksum + hook-timestamp heuristics; 2) performs tenant-scoped incremental CR resync (idempotent apply) limited to suspected namespaces to avoid cluster-wide reconciliation storms; 3) introduces a leader-backed per-tenant semaphore to prevent thundering herd when many tenants remap simultaneously; 4) emits targeted telemetry (reconcile-duration, orphaned-kv-count, applied-fix-version) for post-deploy validation. Trade-offs: we avoid full cluster snapshot/restore (too slow) and we accept a temporary 2-minute per-tenant resync window to minimize blast radius.
acceptance_criteria:
- Operator 2.7.4 deployed to canary rack with zero regression on synthetic upgrade tests.
- Escalated customer confirmed sustained traffic after hotfix for 1 full hour.
- Telemetry shows orphaned-kv-count down to zero for affected tenants within resync window.
- Unit and e2e tests cover checksum/hook-timestamp detection and semaphore flow.
